title: Las Vegas Travel Guide

hero.alt: Las Vegas Strip skyline at night
hero.headline: Las Vegas Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Beyond the Strip: outdoor escapes, iconic neighborhoods, and high-value day plans.

overview: Las Vegas is known for resort nightlife, but the city is also a strong base for desert landscapes and Southwest road trips. You can split your itinerary between major Strip attractions and nearby outdoor parks.

For first-time travelers, plan one anchor activity each morning and leave afternoons flexible. Distances can be larger than expected, so cluster your days by area: Strip, Downtown, and day-trip zones.
If you want a balanced trip, combine one entertainment-heavy night with one early outdoor day. This keeps energy high while avoiding heat and traffic at peak times.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Best seasons: March to May and October to November
bullets: Spring offers comfortable daytime temperatures for Strip walks and park visits.
Fall brings mild weather and strong conditions for day trips.
Summer is very hot; prioritize early starts and indoor midday plans.
Winter is cooler and often better value for hotels and shows.

travelTips: Hydrate constantly—desert air dries you out quickly, even indoors.
Use rideshare or monorail strategically; walking between resorts can take longer than expected.
Start outdoor activities early to avoid heat and crowds.
If planning multiple day trips, consider a rental car for flexibility.
Check resort fees and parking policies before booking accommodations.
Pack sun protection year-round: hat, sunscreen, and sunglasses.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Las Vegas?
faq.a: Three to four days works well for first-time visitors balancing resorts, Downtown, and one outdoor day trip.

faq.q: What is the best month to visit Las Vegas?
faq.a: April and October are top choices for moderate weather and outdoor flexibility.
Yes, especially with day trips like Red Rock, Hoover Dam, and family-oriented shows or attractions.

faq.q: Do I need a car in Las Vegas?
faq.a: Not for Strip-focused trips, but a car helps if you plan Red Rock, Valley of Fire, or Hoover Dam independently.

faq.q: Can I do Grand Canyon from Las Vegas in one day?
faq.a: Yes. West Rim and some South Rim options run as full-day tours from Las Vegas.

faq.q: Is summer travel to Las Vegas a bad idea?
faq.a: Summer is workable with early starts, indoor midday plans, and strong hydration habits.
